objectives.text: Win the drug war with Washington behind it: cut cocaine output through fumigation, strikes on labs and boats, and extraditions. Abelardo de la Espriella, who won the 21 Jun 2026 runoff by about one point (49.66% to 48.70%), took office on 7 Aug 2026 and promised this line in his inaugural speech, ending Petro's negotiating approach. US officials described the coca and cocaine output as at 'all-time records' in the Sept 2025 decertification memo.

grand_strategy.reading: Colombia changed its partner in 2026 without changing its problem: the cocaine economy and the armed groups on the Venezuelan border are the same, and a hard-line Trump ally sworn in on 7 Aug 2026 has bet that Washington's force can do what negotiation did not. The reset reverses the Petro-era rupture (decertification, sanctions on the president, the tariff war with Ecuador), and the energy lever is back in use, while the Belt and Road pact of May 2025 is a non-binding letter that the new government has not yet addressed in any source found. The paradox is that the rupture cost Colombia its aid and its standing, and the reset buys security cooperation at a price that the policy itself may push across the borders, into Venezuela and Ecuador (an inference, not yet sourced).

stances.note: Partner, warming, since the inauguration of Abelardo de la Espriella on 7 Aug 2026 (he won the 21 Jun 2026 runoff by about one point after Trump endorsed him). Under Petro the relation was ruptured: deportation-flight tariffs answered with tariffs of Colombia's own (Jan 2025), the ambassador recalled (Oct 2025), the decertification (Sep 2025) and the OFAC sanctions on the president (24 Oct 2025). The new government reads the US as its security partner and pledges the Shield of the Americas bloc from its first day: partner, not ally, since no treaty binds the two. Bond - affinity: Plan Colombia, two decades of the closest security tie in South America. The grade rests on tier-3 reporting of the inauguration and on the Treasury record of the rupture (tier 1).

stances.note: Reluctant partner: Colombia cooperates with Caracas on the border out of necessity and resists alignment. After the US strike on Caracas (3 Jan 2026) the ELN pulled back from Venezuela into Catatumbo, and the Petro government threatened joint military action with Venezuela against the group if it did not leave; that is the border cooperation of necessity, not an alliance. Bond - none: no kinship or affinity is documented, the tie is the frontier and the drug routes. The grade rests on one tier-2 research profile of the binational ELN structure and on tier-3 reporting of the January 2026 posture of the Petro government. No source after the 7 Aug 2026 change of government was found: the grade is the previous government's reading, to be re-checked.

stances.note: Rival, warming - a reading, not a label (confidence C, tier-3 sources only). Ecuador announced a 30% security tariff on Colombian imports at Davos (Jan 2026), citing Colombia's lack of reciprocity against drug trafficking on the 600 km border; Bogotá suspended electricity exports on 22 Jan 2026 and imposed reciprocal tariffs. Escalation to 100% from 1 May 2026; Ecuador repealed its 100% tariffs on 31 May 2026 and Colombia followed; electricity exports resumed on 5 Aug 2026. Ecuador keeps the raised fee on Colombian crude through the SOTE pipeline, so the friction is not fully closed. Rival, not adversary: competing interests and open friction, no will to destroy. Bond - none. The 2024-25 frictions named in the brief were not found in the sources; the dispute of record is the 2026 one.

stances_toward.note: Mirror of the COL card, read from Ecuador's side. Ecuador announced a 30% security tariff on Colombian imports in January 2026, citing Colombia's lack of reciprocity against trafficking on the 600 km border. Colombia answered with reciprocal tariffs and a suspension of electricity exports on 22 January 2026. Ecuador raised its tariff to 100% from 1 May 2026 and repealed it on 31 May 2026; electricity resumed on 5 August 2026. Grade: the brief framed Colombia as partner with friction; we grade rival because a tariff war with electricity cut-offs is open economic coercion, the same reading COL makes of Ecuador (C). Warming is the 2026 de-escalation. Bond none is our reading. Gaps: the 2024-25 border and gang frictions are not sourced here; the SOTE transit fee on Colombian crude is in the COL card only, from one Spanish-language report.

stances_toward.note: A partner recovered by changing the partner. Under Petro Washington went as far as it goes short of war: deportation-flight tariffs (Jan 2025), the chargé recalled (Jul), Petro's visa revoked (Sep), OFAC sanctions on the president himself (24 Oct 2025), aid ended, 'watch his ass' after Caracas (3 Jan 2026), then an invitation to the White House five days later. With de la Espriella elected on 22 Jun 2026 after Trump's endorsement, the posture is the Shield-of-the-Americas model: a 'regional champion' against cartels. Partner, not ally: the major non-NATO ally status is a designation, no treaty. Warming since the election. Bond - affinity: Plan Colombia, two decades of the closest security tie in South America. Colombia has no card yet.

stances_toward.note: Partner across a border under strain. Petro met Rodriguez in person in Caracas on 24 April 2026 (the first in-person meeting, AP) on the Catatumbo armed groups, intelligence and gas, after a border meeting planned for March was called off. Abelardo de la Espriella took office on 7 Aug 2026 and said in the campaign that Bogota would not deal directly with the chavista government, only through the US State Department; Rodriguez congratulated him and asked that the past be left behind. Partner because the border needs dealings; not ally, no treaty. Stable because the new government has taken no step yet, the stance is for the government in office. Bond none. Confidence C: the Colombian stance is still being formed, and Petro's affinity is no longer Bogota's policy. Mirror: none yet (the COL card is not written).
